S.1 Audited Source Set and Audit Scope

The audited source set consists of sources that state uses of time in classical mechanics, relativity, quantum theory, thermal and statistical physics, gravitation and cosmology, quantum gravity, emergence and information theory, and measurement and standards. Each source as of August 2026 is identified by its formal bibliographic record and the original source under audit.

Definition S.1 (Finite audited source set).

The finite set of the 72 sources under audit,

𝖱𝖾𝖿audit,|𝖱𝖾𝖿audit|=72\mathsf{Ref}^{\mathrm{audit}}\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak\qquad\left|\mathsf{% Ref}^{\mathrm{audit}}\right|=72

is called the finite audited source set.

This set is the source quantification domain of the source-specific and cross-source audits. Each

R∈𝖱𝖾𝖿auditR\in\mathsf{Ref}^{\mathrm{audit}}

is associated with a formal bibliographic record, the original source under audit, and structured source locations corresponding to its principal claims.

Section 7 gives the general audit method for determining use of time within laws, primitive-time premises, and time-generation obligations. This supplement gives the source-specific audit obtained by applying that method to every member of the finite audited source set and the cross-source comparisons obtained from the audit family.

S.1.1 Classification of Time-Order-Structure Content

The audited source set, the time contents of individual sources, the time content of all audited sources, the results of individual sources, the transfer events of individual sources, and the time-content inputs of transfer events and results are as specified in Definitions 7.1 and 7.4 .

The five-type classification of time content and the eight-axis classification of temporal order structure are as specified in Definitions 7.20 and 7.21 . The following tables give the source-wise inverse images of the two classification maps.

The component order of each five-type inverse-image index-set tuple is: a member of a boundary, stage, or transition-position family; content dependent on the same family; content on a branch outside the boundary; content belonging to a separate requirement family; and lexical or illustrative content.

S.1.2 Transfer Reachability of Time Content and Structural Signatures

Within-reference time-content transfer reachability, the member structural signature, and the dependent-content structural signature are given, respectively, by Definitions 7.5, 7.23 and 7.24 .

The zero fiber of the member structural signature,

∐R∈𝖱𝖾𝖿audit({R}×(𝖲𝗂𝗀Rtime,ord,struct,member)−1⁢({(0,0,0)}))\displaystyle\coprod_{R\in\mathsf{Ref}^{\mathrm{audit}}}\left(\{R\}\times\left% (\mathsf{Sig}^{\mathrm{time\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak ord\mathchar 44\relax% \allowbreak struct\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak member}}_{R}\right)^{-1}\left(% \left\{(0\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak 0\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak 0)\right% \}\right)\right)

contains 69 entries. Each corresponds to an evidentiary location in an original-source definition, equation, or explicit statement that provides an endpoint, instant, interval boundary, phase boundary, turning position, order relation, orientation, or transition position.

The zero fiber of the dependent-content structural signature,

∐R∈𝖱𝖾𝖿audit({R}×(𝖲𝗂𝗀Rtime,ord,struct,dependency)−1⁢({(0,0,0)}))\displaystyle\coprod_{R\in\mathsf{Ref}^{\mathrm{audit}}}\left(\{R\}\times\left% (\mathsf{Sig}^{\mathrm{time\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak ord\mathchar 44\relax% \allowbreak struct\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak dependency}}_{R}\right)^{-1}% \left(\left\{(0\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak 0\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak 0)% \right\}\right)\right)

contains 133 entries. Each corresponds to an evidentiary location in an original-source definition, equation, or explicit statement that provides a clock, coordinate, reference scale, duration, rate, differentiation variable, or representational mediator.

Coverage by the five-type classification of time content, totality of the eight-axis classification for members, unique decomposition of structural signatures, and correspondence of zero fibers to original-source evidence are established, respectively, by Propositions 7.195, 7.196, 7.197 and 7.198 .

S.1.3 Audit-Boundary Directed Hypergraphs

Audit-boundary directed hypergraphs are given by Definition 7.27.

The physical and mathematical boundary claims, time contents, transfer events, and reference-specific results stated in each reference are represented by a finite directed hypergraph for that reference. The input set of each hyperedge represents the set of premises used jointly to establish its output.

Audit-boundary nodes, audit-boundary support sets, and audit-boundary edges are given by Definition 7.18 and Definition 7.26.

Input consistency of audit-boundary directed hypergraphs is established by Proposition 7.122.

S.1.4 Reachability on the Audit-Boundary Directed Hypergraph

Audit reachability stages, audit-generation traces, input influence regions, and audit-generated time contents, primitive time roots, and audit-generated results are given by Definition 7.30, Proposition 7.31, Definition 7.32, Definition 7.34, and Definition 7.39.

S.1.5 Result Dependence on Primitive Time Roots

The decomposition of reference-specific results by dependence on primitive time roots is given by Proposition 7.49.
